about: Jean Manciat farms about five and a half hectares around Charnay-lès-Mâcon, on the western edge of Mâcon in southern Burgundy, with a few parcels in Saint-Véran and Pouilly-Fuissé. The Mâconnais is dominated by cooperatives and négociants, and Manciat’s family once sold to the Charnay co-op. When he took over the estate he left it to bottle under his own name, replanting where he had to but keeping as many old vines as he could.

He farms like a Côte d’Or grower rather than a Mâconnais one: Chardonnay is pruned short in the Guyot style, yields stay under 50 hectolitres per hectare (roughly half of what co-op growers routinely harvest), grapes are picked by hand, and grass is sown between rows instead of using herbicides. For the Mâcon-Charnay, whole clusters are pressed straight away and fermented with native yeasts in stainless steel. The wine rests on its fine lees in tank, sees no oak at all, and is lightly filtered before bottling.

Grown on clay and limestone, the wine is about fruit and stone rather than wood. Expect fruity, floral aromas, orchard fruit and citrus, with a flinty minerality and a saline finish. Manciat does use oak, some of it new, for his Vieilles Vignes and Saint-Véran, so leaving this cuvée in steel is a deliberate choice to show the village and the vintage. The warm 2023 season gave it a little more texture and ripeness than usual.
facts: Whole-cluster pressed, native-yeast fermentation in stainless steel
On fine lees in steel tank, no oak
